newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Weak escudo means Portugal rate cut unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Weak escudo means Portugal rate cut unlikely.

text.p: The weak escudo is the main reason why the Bank of Portugal is expected to refrain from cutting official rates next week, economists said.
Seven economists polled by Reuters said they believed that the Bank of Portugal would leave its official rates unchanged on Monday on the eve of a new commercial bank reserve period.
"There are problems in the mark-peseta exchange rate, which limits scope for the Bank of Portugal to cut rates," said Jorge Ferraz of IMF-Informacao de Mercados Financeiros.

The escudo hovered around 100.30 per mark on Friday after the Bank of Portugal sold marks around that level to prevent a slide in the Portuguese currency, which has tracked the peseta against the mark.
Earlier this month the escudo hit lows against the mark around 99.30 per mark.
Economists said that the Bank of Portugal may be inclined to wait for the release of January inflation figures before acting to ease rates.

"The Bank of Portugal will have to wait for money rates, which have risen recently, to calm down, for the January inflation numbers and for renewed stability in the escudo," said Joao Miguel Lourenco of broker Siemca.
Portuguese medium money rates are now about 20 basis points (bp) above the lows registered in the middle of January.
The repurchase pact rate is presently 6.50 percent, the absorption rate used to drain funds from the money market is 6.20 percent and the emergency lending rate is 8.30 percent.
All seven economists said they believed that the Bank of Portugal had room to cut rates further this year.

"The scope for further rate cuts in Portugal is limited because inflation in most European countries could rise early this year, especially because of the recent increase in oil prices, bad weather and the truck drivers' strike in France," said Cristina Casalinho of Banco Portugues de Investimento.
